text:
Anya: Quick sync — we need the benchmark narrative locked for the Tue webinar. Primary hooks: predictable cost, latency guarantees, and what customers should expect in routing. brainstorm pls :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Darin: 3-panel approach works well: 1) median latency vs prompt size, 2) unit cost (tokens) across batching strategies, 3) tail-latency percentiles with fallback behavior. short bullets for slides.
Maya: I can mock visuals for those panels. prefer a small-multiples layout so we can compare models and Dedicated vs Hosted. will share comps by EOD.
Ken: data note — our test suite uses 8k seq dist: 70% <1k, 25% 1-4k, 5% >4k. callout that quantized model runs skew cost in specific buckets.
Anya: good — include a tiny table or overlay that explains the sequence distribution. audiences get confused if we only show averages.
Darin: inbound routing CTA — capture leads from 'capacity-sensitive' and 'latency-sensitive' buckets. propose two routing tags: "dedicated-interest" and "low-latency-trial".
Lina: for sales: please include sample qualification copy. short: "Are you optimizing for cost per 1k tokens or strict tail latency?" That maps to routing.
Maya: mock headline options: 1) "Predictable inference economics" 2) "Latency you can commit to" 3) "Scale without surprises" Thoughts?
Darin: prefer 1 & 2 combo across hero + subhead. hero: "Predictable inference economics" subhead: "Commit to latency SLAs and control cost at scale."
Ken: one technical caveat we should add as footnote: batching benefits vary heavily by request heterogeneity and KV cache hit rates. include a short example: `Batching reduced per-token cost by 2.3x on uniform short prompts, but only 1.1x with mixed lengths.`
Anya: agree — call that out as a tooltip on the cost chart. also need a small faq card: "Why does Dedicated show lower cost but sometimes higher median latency?" brief answer: resource isolation + different autoscale windows.
Maya: design question — should we show raw numbers or normalized indexes? raw numbers are punchier for sales decks, index is better for technical blog. we can do both: raw on slides, index in appendix.
bench-bot: test-run results posted: https://internal/bench/2134 — median/95/99 for host/dedicated/quantized.
Darin: nice. Maya, can you incorporate those concrete numbers into the slides? Anya, can you draft the short webinar copy and registration form text? Lina, I'll send routing rules once copy's done.
Anya: I'll draft the registration blurbs now. rough: "Join us for a 30-min deep dive into benchmarking inference economics — see real numbers, tradeoffs, and routing strategies that save engineering time." will post first draft in ~90m.
Lina: For lead routing, proposed rule snippet (pseudocode):
```
if answer == 'cost' -> add_tag('dedicated-interest')
if answer == 'tail_latency' -> add_tag('low-latency-trial')
if company_size > 500 -> route_to('enterprise-sales')
else -> route_to('growth-nurture')
```
Anya: perfect. also add a checkbox for "I want a Private deployment consult" to capture regulated buyers.
Ken: one more data ask — can we include cost-per-1k-tokens table for the 3 leading quant configs? I'll run and update bench-bot results.
Maya: timeline check — mock slides by EOD, final slides by Mon noon, rehearsal Tue 10am. everyone ok?
Darin: I can do routing automation before Tue 6pm.
Lina: sales playbook bullets by Mon afternoon from me.
Anya: deadline noted. thanks team — I'll post the registration copy in 90m and circle back with a TL;DR doc that we can paste into the webinar landing page. :memo:
